last_attempts_log.asr_text: Meanwhile, U.S. consumer price data showed that the price of coffee was 6.1% higher than in the same month a year earlier. It may leave you wondering, did prices go down or up? But the data covers a different month from the bean price measure, and it does not show the price of a cup at a cafe. Hold on before putting the two figures in the ring. So how long does it take for the price of beans to reach a price tag? According to estimates from market insiders and experts interviewed by Reuters, it takes at least about nine months for the price of raw beans to show up in U.S. retail prices. The road to a price tag is quite a long journey. The article says that companies in the U.S. that roast coffee keep raw beans in stock. Roasting and packing the beans also take time. They also often negotiate prices with retailers on a regular basis. The price tag in a shop does not flash to a new price the moment the market moves.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: However, the about nine months figure is an estimate based on interviews. It is not a rule that applies to every company, and it is not a promise that prices will fall in nine months. It is too soon to mark the date on your calendar. And a cup at a cafe comes with costs besides the beans. One cafe operator in Chicago said that the cost of cups and labor, as well as the cost of buying beans, had been behind price increases. Even if bean prices fall, other costs do not always fall along with them. If you are waiting for the price of your usual cup to come down, think not only “How much do beans cost now?” but also “When does the price of the beans reach here?” A coffee price tag may have an unseen clock of its own, separate from the latest news about the market.
